summary: P1b session-expiry recovery bridge tested end-to-end on PWQ, GenericToolPage (Price Work Profit), cross-tool isolation, stale-snapshot cleanup, and security. 4 of 5 scenarios PASS. SCENARIO 2 FAILS: GenericToolPage restores the snapshot into state momentarily (restore toast fires + snapshot is consumed + cleared) but the field values render as EMPTY and conditional dependsOn fields (unitRate, unitsCompleted) disappear — a useEffect race in GenericToolPage.jsx wipes `values` after the recovery useEffect sets them. Scenario 6 (multi-tab) skipped per spec.

ui_bugs.issue: Session-recovery restore is functionally broken: snapshot is consumed, toast fires ('Restored your unsaved Price Work Profit Calculator from before you signed out.'), localStorage key is cleared — but all field inputs render EMPTY. `field-pricingBasis` is blank so the dependsOn conditional fields `field-unitRate` and `field-unitsCompleted` are not visible either. The bug reproduces 100% on /app/tool/pricework-profit after a 401 → re-login flow. Snapshot payload itself is correct (values.jobTitle, values.pricingBasis='Per Item / Piece', values.unitRate='45', values.unitsCompleted='120' all present in localStorage before consume).

action_items: Fix the useEffect race in /app/frontend/src/pages/GenericToolPage.jsx between the tool-init effect (line 85, `setValues(init)`) and the session-recovery effect (line 156, `setValues(d.values)`). Both share deps `[toolId, tool]` but the observed behaviour is that `setValues(init)` wins — either because a second render re-runs the init effect while the recovery effect is guarded off by `recoveryConsumedFor`, or because effect ordering / batching is producing an unexpected final commit. Recommended fix: (a) merge recovery-consume INTO the same effect as the init reset (consume first, then only apply defaults for fields the snapshot did not carry), OR (b) use a `didRestoreFor` ref and skip the `setValues(init)` in the init effect when a snapshot exists for this toolId, OR (c) call `consumeRecoverySnapshot(toolId)` synchronously during initial useState via a lazy initializer so it wins the first paint deterministically. Same class of fix should be applied to the `liveSignature`/`clientSignature`/`attachedPhotos` resets on line 97-98 which also compete with the recovery setters.

Consider also fixing the ORDER guarantee: session-recovery useEffect should run AFTER any reset useEffect. Currently init effect and recovery effect share the same deps and declaration order means init runs first — but any subsequent render (e.g. from useAuth `refresh`, tool metadata reload, or React 18 concurrent re-render) will re-run init and NOT re-run recovery (blocked by ref guard), which wipes the restored values.
critical_code_review_comments: GenericToolPage.jsx line 85-121: The tool-init useEffect unconditionally sets values, result, refNumber, liveSignature, clientSignature, attachedPhoto, attachedPhotos to empty on every [toolId, tool] fire. This is fundamentally incompatible with the session-recovery effect at line 156-170 which tries to set the same state a moment later. The recovery guard prevents re-consume but not re-reset. Merge the two effects OR add a `recoverySnapshotPending` ref set synchronously (peek without consume) that the init effect can inspect and skip its resets.

PriceWorkQuote.jsx does not exhibit this bug because its state is initialised via `useState('PW-001')` etc. — no separate reset effect competes with the recovery effect. The GenericToolPage architecture (values-as-a-single-object) requires a different restore strategy.
session-recovery.js is sound. Isolation, TTL, single-slot semantics, and consume-and-clear behaviour all validated by scenarios 3 and 4.

rca of the issue: GenericToolPage session-recovery race. Both the tool-init useEffect (line 85) and the session-recovery useEffect (line 156) have dep array [toolId, tool]. In the primary mount cycle they run in declaration order: init first (setValues(init)), recovery second (setValues(d.values)) — the batched commit should therefore land on d.values. Observed behaviour, however, is that field inputs render empty AND the restore toast still fires, which means the recovery effect DID execute setValues(d.values) but a subsequent render restored the empty init state. The most likely trigger is a second render pass in which the init effect re-fires (or was scheduled after the recovery commit) while the recovery effect is blocked by the `recoveryConsumedFor.current === toolId` guard. React 18 concurrent rendering, useAuth `user`/`refresh` updates, or the tool object being memoised by identity via getToolById could all produce this second pass. Mitigation options listed in action_items. Reproduction: login as darrenhustle300 → /app/tool/pricework-profit → fill all fields incl. pricingBasis='Per Item / Piece' → corrupt token → click Generate → login again → /app/tool/pricework-profit. Toast appears but every field is blank.
